reported_red_green_and_check_lines.text: Twelve assigned findings are repaired in this branch, five are repaired in part with explicit ownership handoffs, and two formatting findings remain assigned to the report/charts worker. The handoffs must be combined before the corresponding canonical finding can be closed.

| C1-008 | repaired | Library cards show admitted delivery state, sector rather than raw issuer ID, and the exact designated credit-view paragraph. A compact additive `lead` preserves original paragraph, Basis line, output, hash and line. The card uses existing reader text/reference rules and links its source control to that exact Evidence address. Missing lead content is stated, never invented. |
| C1-018 | repaired | Running-card modules show the module name as plain text beside a badge whose visible word is the state. |
| C1-019 | repaired | Query, sector, pathway and Cards/List choice live in search parameters and are restored on a fresh mount. Other address parameters and history state remain intact. |
| C1-022 | repaired | The search, sector and pathway labels use the same type, colour and spacing classes; the search retains its width limit. |

| C1-027 | repaired | Spend, settled charges, holds and cap round their original decimal strings half up to cents. Binary numbers are used only for bar geometry. Decimal and exponent spellings agree; zero/underflow exponents do not allocate enormous powers. |

| C1-028 | repaired | The existing report metadata request carries designated outputs explicitly marked Not assessable/unreadable. Run progress displays their assessment state while retaining completed-module counts and the separate report-delivery step. The original checker-stop handling remains. Older metadata with no field remains readable. No extra HTTP request is made. |
| J1-008 | repaired | The tally says `Ended without a report`. A populated page links to the library; the empty state retains its library action and explanation. |

| J1-011 | repaired | The connected rail says `Run activity`; its existing NavButton tooltip receives that same label. The shared current area also gains the distinct line marker required by S1-019. |

| J2-009 | repaired | Under the retained `Start from this run` control, the page explicitly says it opens a new run with its own cap and leaves the earlier run as it is. No resume/retry control was added (OQ-06). |
| J2-010 | repaired | An ended run's feed has its recorded terminal state, reason and end time ahead of earlier Running entries. A live run has no invented end entry. |

| J2-015 | repaired | Where no specific run/held reason exists, queued rows and progress explain that the run waits for a slot and starts when the service can accept it. Existing specific reasons remain. No unsupported live count or queue position is invented. |
| S6-037 | repaired | The progress card is explicitly `Modules and report delivery`, consistent with the analytical-module count excluding Report. |

| J4-001 | in part | The new credit-view paragraph has an exact source control. Individual library-card metric traces require the group-2 HeadlineFigures/report worker; no guessed metric provenance was added. |

| Card paragraph/source-control additions | 2 failures before rendering the new source-preserving card credit view. |
| `Shell.finalAudit.test.tsx` | 2 failures for marker/connected label; nullable-current runtime guard already passed. Type checking also required nullable current support. |
| `tests/test_react_library_cards.py`, initial compact lead cases | 5 failures, with the no-wrong-pathway guard already passing. |
| C1-028 published blocked metadata | Python 1 failure and UI 1 failure before the additive metadata and display handling; older-metadata guard already passed. |
| `ConnectedApp.loading.test.tsx` | Skeleton assertion failed first; a later loading-destination title assertion also failed before its title effect. |
| `tests/test_react_run_reason_sentences.py` | 1 failure for `. daily`, with the unchanged unrecognised-message guard already passing. |

| Confidence check of blocked-status semantics | 1 failure: a preceding nonempty level-three audit section must use the reader's legacy declared-status fallback. The helper now follows that existing rule exactly. |

| C1-018 | repaired | Running-card modules show the module name as plain text beside a badge whose visible word is the state. |
| C1-019 | repaired | Query, sector, pathway and Cards/List choice live in search parameters and are restored on a fresh mount. Other address parameters and history state remain intact. |
| C1-022 | repaired | The search, sector and pathway labels use the same type, colour and spacing classes; the search retains its width limit. |

| C1-027 | repaired | Spend, settled charges, holds and cap round their original decimal strings half up to cents. Binary numbers are used only for bar geometry. Decimal and exponent spellings agree; zero/underflow exponents do not allocate enormous powers. |

| C1-028 | repaired | The existing report metadata request carries designated outputs explicitly marked Not assessable/unreadable. Run progress displays their assessment state while retaining completed-module counts and the separate report-delivery step. The original checker-stop handling remains. Older metadata with no field remains readable. No extra HTTP request is made. |
| J1-008 | repaired | The tally says `Ended without a report`. A populated page links to the library; the empty state retains its library action and explanation. |

| J1-011 | repaired | The connected rail says `Run activity`; its existing NavButton tooltip receives that same label. The shared current area also gains the distinct line marker required by S1-019. |

| J2-009 | repaired | Under the retained `Start from this run` control, the page explicitly says it opens a new run with its own cap and leaves the earlier run as it is. No resume/retry control was added (OQ-06). |
| J2-010 | repaired | An ended run's feed has its recorded terminal state, reason and end time ahead of earlier Running entries. A live run has no invented end entry. |

| J2-015 | repaired | Where no specific run/held reason exists, queued rows and progress explain that the run waits for a slot and starts when the service can accept it. Existing specific reasons remain. No unsupported live count or queue position is invented. |
| S6-037 | repaired | The progress card is explicitly `Modules and report delivery`, consistent with the analytical-module count excluding Report. |

The handoffs must be combined before the corresponding canonical finding can be closed.

| C1-008 | repaired | Library cards show admitted delivery state, sector rather than raw issuer ID, and the exact designated credit-view paragraph. A compact additive `lead` preserves original paragraph, Basis line, output, hash and line. The card uses existing reader text/reference rules and links its source control to that exact Evidence address. Missing lead content is stated, never invented. |
| C1-018 | repaired | Running-card modules show the module name as plain text beside a badge whose visible word is the state. |
| C1-019 | repaired | Query, sector, pathway and Cards/List choice live in search parameters and are restored on a fresh mount. Other address parameters and history state remain intact. |
| C1-022 | repaired | The search, sector and pathway labels use the same type, colour and spacing classes; the search retains its width limit. |

| C1-027 | repaired | Spend, settled charges, holds and cap round their original decimal strings half up to cents. Binary numbers are used only for bar geometry. Decimal and exponent spellings agree; zero/underflow exponents do not allocate enormous powers. |

| C1-028 | repaired | The existing report metadata request carries designated outputs explicitly marked Not assessable/unreadable. Run progress displays their assessment state while retaining completed-module counts and the separate report-delivery step. The original checker-stop handling remains. Older metadata with no field remains readable. No extra HTTP request is made. |
| J1-008 | repaired | The tally says `Ended without a report`. A populated page links to the library; the empty state retains its library action and explanation. |

| J1-011 | repaired | The connected rail says `Run activity`; its existing NavButton tooltip receives that same label. The shared current area also gains the distinct line marker required by S1-019. |

| J2-009 | repaired | Under the retained `Start from this run` control, the page explicitly says it opens a new run with its own cap and leaves the earlier run as it is. No resume/retry control was added (OQ-06). |
| J2-010 | repaired | An ended run's feed has its recorded terminal state, reason and end time ahead of earlier Running entries. A live run has no invented end entry. |

| J2-015 | repaired | Where no specific run/held reason exists, queued rows and progress explain that the run waits for a slot and starts when the service can accept it. Existing specific reasons remain. No unsupported live count or queue position is invented. |
| S6-037 | repaired | The progress card is explicitly `Modules and report delivery`, consistent with the analytical-module count excluding Report. |

| J4-001 | in part | The new credit-view paragraph has an exact source control. Individual library-card metric traces require the group-2 HeadlineFigures/report worker; no guessed metric provenance was added. |

Additional coordinated changes: S1-019's shared rail marker; S1-011's `Shell.current: Area | null` support for the static not-found worker; the real service `Run.stopped_by` field replaces the hidden local intersection; optional filed `issuer_name` and `approved_summary_limits` API types support the start/evidence workers. T03's joined rebuild/daily-limit notice now starts the second sentence `Daily`, preserving the rest exactly.

separate_ruledout.expected: CM-088 and CT-011 (the run's currency is the currency of the source statements; not asked, defaulted or read); retired R-18 (no reporting-currency question).
separate_ruledout.actual: The row is a read-out, not a question, and the page does not ask for the currency; the matrix says 'not shown'. No US$m label or non-USD warning is drawn.
separate_ruledout.remaining_required_action: No repair required under the recorded ruling/scope; reviewed already-merged fixes stay.

separate_ruledout.title: Parts of the static run screens that no matrix row accounts for: Readiness panel, the More context free-text step, run header chips (pathway, as-of) and status badge, the activity feed, the Elapsed figure, the unreadable-activity state, the not-found and no-run empty states, the saved-example notice, the Approval badge and the Run started panel.
separate_ruledout.ruling_note: OQ-13 decided (R10): keep each item; the matrix rows are added in harmony.md
separate_ruledout.expected: Brief check 4 (list what the screens show that no matrix row accounts for).
separate_ruledout.actual: None of these has a row in content-matrix.csv or control-matrix.csv with S6 in section_id (CM-083 names the stepper and rows of Documents; CM-089 and CM-090 name module progress and scope).
separate_ruledout.remaining_required_action: No repair required under the recorded ruling/scope; reviewed already-merged fixes stay.

separate_ruledout.title: Rows for controls that exist only on the connected page or in the launching environment have no counterpart on the static run screens: the synthetic Submit (CT-033), the Submit retry message (CT-037) and the Teams run cards (CT-042). The R8 question for the Teams POST is still open (harmony-report H-26).
separate_ruledout.ruling_note: OQ-11 decided (R10): the Teams card POST is a recorded exception (R8, R10)
separate_ruledout.expected: CT-033, CT-037, CT-042; README R8 (only the live model run and CP-DR lookups leave the machine).
separate_ruledout.actual: None of the S6 screens makes a request to any host but the local machine (0 blocked requests over all addresses, both data variants, and the connected pages opened with proof.serve); the Teams POST is server side, outside these screens. This agent does not settle H-26.
separate_ruledout.remaining_required_action: No repair required under the recorded ruling/scope; reviewed already-merged fixes stay.

separate_ruledout.title: LoadingIndicator hides its visible label from assistive technology and leaves the status region with only a name.
separate_ruledout.ruling_note: R16 (owner, 2026-11-17: 'screen reader - not required'): a finding that changes only what a screen reader announces is not a defect; any reviewed fix already merged stays
separate_ruledout.expected: D-43: a status that appears is exposed in a live region with text a screen reader can announce.
separate_ruledout.actual: The region is <div role='status' aria-label='Waiting for the first module'> whose only text, the label, is aria-hidden='true'; the spinner svg is aria-hidden too, so the region has no text content. Not tried with a screen reader, so whether it announces is not established.
separate_ruledout.remaining_required_action: No repair required under the recorded ruling/scope; reviewed already-merged fixes stay.

   In scripts where a mark is part of the letter, that merges different names. Checked on both sides, with the
   same result: "टाटा" and "टीटी" both give `टट` (Devanagari vowel signs), "ガス" and "カス" both give `カス`

   merged on the default route. This is the round-2 adversarial finding 1 with a smaller reach: CJK, plain
   Cyrillic and Greek names are now told apart (pinned by the new cases). Suggested repair: drop marks only
   where they follow a Latin base letter, or compare on NFKC plus case folding without dropping marks. Either
   way, keep the same rule on both sides.

Observation, not a finding: Greek final sigma means "ΟΣ-ΑΕ" and "ΟΣΑΕ" give different keys (`οςαε` / `οσαε`) on
both sides. This errs on the safe side: the same issuer is refused, not merged.

1. Low, `web/src/pages/connected/ReportContent.tsx:591` (observation, for the controller or owner; not a defect of this change). On a data module (CP-0, CP-1 in the canned run) the figures are drawn straight after the Bottom line and before the tables: CP-0 Bottom line, figures (351 px), "Readiness by area"; CP-1 Bottom line, seven charts (1,638 px), "Financials and credit metrics" (about 1,700 px down). Judged against the three sources:
   - OQ-02 (figures after the prose passages, before Limitations): met literally. A data module owes only the Bottom line, so there is no later prose passage and no Limitations to come before.
   - CM-006 (data modules owe the Bottom line, "their tables follow as the main content"): the tables follow the Bottom line, after the figures. The matrix does not say whether figures or tables come first.
   - CM-005 reads "Limitations, then typed records, figures and tables", which would put tables before figures. OQ-02 already overrides CM-005 for prose modules, where records follow Limitations and the figures precede it. CM-005 and the header of p19 still describe the pre-ruling order and should be amended by the lead.
   - The order for CP-0 and CP-1 is the same as on the base, so nothing regressed and no prose passage is pushed down. If the owner wants tables first on data modules, it is a one-line change: for a module that owes only the Bottom line, place the figures after the other sections (`figuresAt`). The guard test "draws the figures ahead of the other sections when only the bottom line is owed" would then change.

### N1 detail (joined held note)

The scheduler joins its held notes with `"; "` in this order: rebuild, daily limit, unreadable
(`scheduler.py:471`). `_REBUILD_NOTE.sub` consumes the first `"; "` and puts one space after the
mapped sentence. Through `_shown`:

```
rebuild + limit:      "...ask whoever runs the service to check the service's log. daily limit of 30 runs reached; waiting until tomorrow"
rebuild + unreadable: "...check the service's log. 1 run record could not be read. Its run is not started, ..."   (reads correctly: a digit)
rebuild + limit + unreadable: "...service's log. daily limit of 30 runs reached; waiting until tomorrow; 1 run record could not be read. ..."
rebuild alone:        "...check the service's log."   (reads correctly)
```

A reader takes the lower-case tail as a second notice with no end stop; it is understandable, and
the daily-limit note already starts in lower case when it stands alone in the same alert, so this
is the existing style meeting a new capital. Rated Low, not Medium: it needs a persistent rebuild
failure and a day at the 30-run limit (`Settings.max_per_day`), nothing is wrong or misleading, and
the unreadable-record note, the more likely partner, reads correctly. The fix, if wanted:
`(?P<more>; (?P<head>.))?` and `+ (" " + note["head"].upper() if note["more"] else "")`. The
implementer's alternative (a trailing `;`) is rightly rejected: it would leave the usual
single-note case with no full stop.
